The Ti66.8V11.2Al9.6Zr6.2Nb6.2 (at.%) LRCCA was initially prepared via vacuum arc melting under high-purity argon atmosphere.
during the melting process, we performed nine successive remelting cycles to ensure chemical homogeneity of the alloy.
The as-cast button ingot was then hot-rolled at 800 ◦C with approximately 30 % reduction
followed by annealing at 800 ◦C for 1 h
Subsequently, the alloy sheet underwent cold rolling with about 80 % reduction.
The cold-rolled sheet was subjected to recrystallization treatment at 740 ◦C for 15 min.
All heat-treated samples were water-quenched.
Samples were then extracted from the recrystallized sheet using wire electrical discharge machining for subsequent aging treatments at 580 ◦C with varying durations.
the hardness of the alloy reaches its peak after 6 h of aging
Phase mapping analysis in Fig. 5 c confirms that the Re alloy consists exclusively of a single BCC solid solution phase
The results reveal a dual-phase BCC + HCP microstructure without deformation twins

attributes.location: both within grain interiors and along grain boundaries

evidence.quote: Quantitative phase analysis reveals that the volume fraction of precipitates is approximately 9.2 %, with fine lath-like precipitates distributed both within grain interiors and along grain boundaries

The BF image (Fig. 7 a) reveals needle-shaped precipitates formed in the BCC matrix after aging treatment. The corresponding SAED pattern (Fig. 7 b) confirm these precipitates possess an HCP structure
the phase interfaces between the HCP precipitates and the BCC matrix serve as effective barriers and multiplication sources for dislocations
And the EDS mapping results (Fig. 7 f) demonstrates the needle-shaped precipitates are enriched in Ti and Al elements.

attributes.morphology: kinks and bends in the lattice

evidence.quote: there are more kinks and bends in the lattice of the alloys, which indicates that there are serious lattice distortions in the alloys
The Re alloy exhibits numerous parallel slip traces and lamellar deformation bands
The 5◦–19◦ misorientation range excludes the possibility of deformation twins, confirming these features as kink bands
When dislocations propagate to BCC/HCP interfaces, the HCP precipitates strongly impede their motion, leading to significant dislocation pile-ups and tangles at these phase boundaries
The Re alloy demonstrates an excellent strength-ductility trade-off, with a yield strength of approximately 1000 MPa and a fracture strain of about 23 %.

evidence.section: 4.1. Formation of deformation bands and their contribution to ductility
evidence.quote: As strain accumulates, continuous dislocation multiplication and pile-up form dense dislocation networks. These dislocations undergo collective motion and interactions, ultimately developing into slip bands

evidence.section: 4.1. Formation of deformation bands and their contribution to ductility
evidence.quote: The resulting local stress fields drive screw dislocations to rearrange through cross-slip, forming dislocation walls. With progressive deformation, these walls evolve into well-defined substructures, forcing the lattice to undergo shear rotations of 5◦–15◦ in localized regions and eventually forming visible kink bands
the larger-sized precipitates act as hard particles that hinder dislocation motion via the Orowan bypassing mechanism [54]
The grain boundary strengthening contribution to yield strength can be quantified using the classical Hall-Petch equation
the alloy without the precipitates primarily relies on dislocation slip and limited cross-slip to accommodate plastic deformation

evidence.section: 4.1. Formation of deformation bands and their contribution to ductility
evidence.quote: kink bands enhance ductility by locally rotating the lattice and rearranging dislocations, which helps coordinate plastic deformation and relieve stress concentration. This leads to improved fracture strain.
the precipitates not only provide additional strengthening, but more importantly, establish a more sustainable work-hardening capability by promoting dislocation storage and interactions.
solid solution strengthening remains the dominant contributor to the alloy ’ s strength
